title: Do Managers Successfully Shop for Auditors Who Allow Them to Opportunistically Report Positive News? Evidence from Accounting Estimates
authors: Mark L. DeFond; Jieying Zhang; Yuping Zhao
eligible_reason: No qualifying specification. The only DiD (Table 5 Panel C; also the AFTER x DISMISSAL terms in Tables 6-10) compares firms that dismiss their auditor in firm-specific years (2004-2020) with nonswitch firms, but every column uses a pooled treated-group dummy (vs4 = dismissal firm) in place of firm FE, with 12 industry dummies and year dummies, and adds time-varying firm/auditor controls (ta, roa, loss, lev, salegr, mb, big, specialist, logtenure, ...) plus lagged outcomes (lagchgest, lagposchg, lagnegchg). Indicator outcomes are estimated by logit (marginal effects reported); only the magnitude columns are OLS. Tables 6-10 add DDD interactions with continuous/binary estimate-change measures. Tables 3-4 are Lennox (2000) probit shopping models. The text states firm-FE versions are robustness only (not in the package).
design_notes: Treatment: after_vs4 = vs4 x AFTER (three years after dismissal vs three years before), vs4 = dismissal-firm indicator; control group = nonswitch firms. Unit cik/gvkey, time fyear. Clustered by auditor office (auditor_fkey_city). Pooled treated dummy (no firm FE), logit for binary outcomes, lagged outcomes and time-varying controls in every column. Per the Nov 1 rulings a pooled treated-group dummy in place of unit FE does not qualify; with the additional lagged-outcome and nonlinear-model violations this is not coded as a near miss (same as mnsc.2023.4820).
data_files_note: Final firm-year analysis datasets shipped (37,943 firm-years in Tables 5 to 11_MS.dta with cik, gvkey, fyear); underlying sources (Audit Analytics, Compustat) are licensed.
software_notes: Stata (logit, probit, reg with industry/year dummies)
screener_notes: Published PDF read (papers/mnsc/mnsc.2024.05299.pdf, Management Science 71(11), 2025). Section 3 Eq. (1) and Table 5 Panel C confirm industry and year FE only; firm FE mentioned only as an untabulated robustness check.
